Value: Hi!
You must be {AccountData.NickName}, right?
Who are you?
Chilipepper
Someone who's very curious about you.
How did you get my number?
What?
Don't you know?
Well, I didn't think the military academy would tell students about it. Haha.
Military academy graduates are highly sought after.
It's safe to say that you graduates have the attention of all the people in Ark.
Talk about elite, right? Haha.
Not to mention that you can ask Nikkes to do whatever you want.
There are many opportunistic people in the Ark, you know.
Including myself.
So the info of military academy graduates
naturally gets leaked and put up for sale the moment they graduate.
How much?
Cheap.
A lot cheaper than you think.
You'd be surprised.
So I guess I'm not the only one who has the information.
Like I said, there are many opportunistic people in the Ark.
So what are you after?
Whoa.
You're a fast thinker, aren't you?
Elite indeed. Haha.
I need a favor from you.
Remember the place where you did your first mission?
I need you to confirm something there.
Confirm?
Okay.
I'll give you the coordinates.
You should find a ceramic tile that's different from others there.
I need you to confirm what is under that tile.
Ah.
I'll make the trip worth your while.
I do have good conscience, you know. Hahaha.
What do you say? Interested?
All right, I got it.
Oh.
I'll be waiting.
What's their name again? Chilipepper? Chalipepper? Whatever. This is the place she talked about, right?
Yes, the coordinates led us here.
Commander, the floor.
One of the tiles is indeed different from others.
There's a little handle, too. It looks like the tile can be opened.
So should we open it?
I don't feel good about this. Can we trust her?
It doesn't look dangerous.
Hm... That's true.
Then I'll open it.
*Creak*
*Bang*
Ah!
Did I frighten you?
Yes, you did!
Check this out, Commander.
Rapi passes me a wine bottle.
... A wine bottle?
A wine bottle.
Oh, that's boring.
*Bang*
... What the hell?
You said it was boring, so I thought I could spice things up a little.
Well, ain't you clever?
This is your reward.
Reward?
I told you I have a good conscience.
Looks like you have good news.
So what was under there?
A wine bottle.
A wine bottle?
How much wine was in it?
It's a new one.
Argh!
Ahhhhh!
This is annoying. So annoying!
Are you okay?
Yes.
Thanks anyway.
I got a tip for you.
If anyone asks you to do anything without reward, don't do it.
Everyone has to bring food to the table.
If I need anything, I'll tell you.
Oh, right. Do what you want with that bottle of wine.
I have no use for it now.
Bye.
Hello.
I can't stop thinking
about that bottle...
Was there any indication that it'd been opened
or used before?
No, it's completely new.
All right, then.
I'm about to send you some coordinates.
Please make your way there.
You'll be compensated for doing so.
Why do I need to go there?
Umm...
Just to check a few things.
... Actually, I'm not sure.
What should I do after I arrive?
There will be a small building.
Head inside and tell me what you see.
Describe everything to me in detail,
whether it seems important or not.
All right, I'll do it.
Okay.
I'll be waiting.
What's this room?
It looks like... some kind of dormitory?
There's a lot of stuff lying around, but nothing remarkable.
Commander. There is something on the shelf.
Looks like some kind of alcohol.
Yes, but it's different from the last one we saw. This bottle is new as well.
What's it doing here though?
That, I don't know.
Anyone else has any ideas? I'm all ears.
Chilipepper could be a hard drinker.
Oh yea! Why did I not think of that?
Should we take this with us?
Yes, let's take it for now.
Roger that.
Well done.
This one is new as well.
This is too much...
Care to explain?
Well, actually...
the place I told you about
was some temporary accommodation where my father used to stay.
He was a construction manager at the Outpost.
He was always heading up to the surface to gather materials.
Outpost construction manager?
Yes.
The Outpost was a gargantuan project.
Building yet another underground city
on top of a pre-existing one was a massive undertaking.
They intended on building an underground base that was closer to the surface than the Ark.
Given the large scope of the project,
many people were jockeying for the position.
My father eventually secured the position by greasing a few palms.
But the Outpost was never finished.
That's correct.
Do you remember how I said the goal was to build a base closer to the surface?
Well, they ended up getting too close.
Raptures started to come down.
The Outpost was originally meant to be a hub that connects the Ark and the surface,
but as the Raptures spilled in, everything degenerated into chaos.
Only two elevators managed to emerge unscathed.
One going up to the surface, and another connecting to the Ark.
All construction was halted.
That's why this place has become what it is now.
What about the alcohol?
I gave
them to my father
as a way to apologize.
But he didn't even open it,
doesn't this mean he doesn't accept my apology?
Was there a rift between you two?
Not really.
Well, in a way. But it was one-sided.
I said all sorts of terrible things to him.
Hmm...
For a moment, Chilipepper falls silent.
Anyway, good job.
I still would like to know where my father's final resting place is.
I'll think it over and contact you later.
Bye.
Hello.
This should be my last request.
Proceed to the coordinates I've sent,
and confirm if the bottle is empty or not.
How are you sure there will be a bottle there?
I met with some of my father's old friends.
They said he took a bottle of booze with him everywhere he went.
The drink names match as well.
So it should be there.
... That place is also where my father died.
Is that everything you can tell me?
Would telling you more be helpful?
Of course.
Hmm...
Chilipepper doesn't say anything for a long time.
Constructing the Outpost
was a herculean effort. Time-consuming and complicated.
Whenever he wasn't working, my father's routine consisted entirely of getting drunk and sleeping.
He never gave me so much as a second glance.
I had to endure that for 10 long years, and I resented him for it.
One day, I couldn't take it anymore,
and I screamed that if he dropped dead, I wouldn't shed a tear.
If anything, I'd end up vomiting
because his corpse would reek of booze.
Something along those lines.
I left home and cut all ties with my father.
I never considered that those drinks he had after work
were his one and only solace.
A few years later, when construction was nearly finished,
I understood my father more than I did before.
I couldn't bring myself to apologize to his face,
so I bought him a set of whiskey.
I figured if he was willing to drink all of it, and bring back the empty bottle,
it would in some way show that he'd forgiven me.
I wanted to join him, but I can't drink.
One day, he went up to gather materials
and never returned.
Eventually, I saw his name on a list of casualties.
Sigh...
So that's my story.
I just hope, at the very end...
that my father was able to forgive me.
Not that we'll ever find anything.
I'm sure we will.
That would be the best.
I'll wait for an update from you.
I found the beer bottle.
How does it look like?
... Unopened.
... Right.
Something's not right.
Yes. Why place the bottle here in the first place if you're not going to drink it?
Maybe he was funny in the head or something.
Hmm? Everyone, look at this.
What's that?
... Non-alcoholic beer.
Non-alcoholic? Wait, as in zero alcohol?
Yes.
Can you even call that beer?
I guess some people just enjoy the taste.
So you get the taste of beer without getting drunk... Interesting.
Chilipepper can't drink.
Maybe his father wanted to share a drink with his son, and this stuff would let him do that.
But then why would he have the bottle as well?
Maybe he wasn't sure
whether he wanted to forgive Chilipepper or not.
Or maybe he never intended on forgiving him.
Hmm...
Hmm...
There's no way of knowing the truth, is there?
I suppose you're right.
But it's so frustrating.
Wouldn't a phone call solve everything, though?
I'm sorry, I forgive you, or even I don't forgive you.
You're right.
Here is your final payment.
You've done an outstanding job.
But...
I must ask...
for your opinion
whether you think my father has ever forgiven me?
Yes, he did.
No, he didn't.
Really?
Do you really think so?
That would be truly amazing.
Sigh...
I wouldn't have either.
A son who doesn't think about anyone except himself...
I hope...
you can make good use of the Outpost.
Although incomplete, it is still my father's creation.
He was an incredibly gifted man.
We will.
Argh!
It's not fair!
What I would give to see him one last time...
*Knock knock*
Anyone there?
Who are you?
Oh, hello.
I'm just someone who's scraping by in the Outer Rim.
The Outer Rim?
What's the matter?
Don't you know?
The Outer Rim is the fringe of the Ark.
The outskirts of Ark.
Life in the Ark is pretty convenient, right?
Haha, the Outer Rim is like hell.
There's no place to eat, sleep, or work.
That place is not for humans.
I've heard about you and what you did, Commander.
So I think perhaps you can help me live like a human.
I know this may be abrupt, but I had to contact you.
Whoa.
Straight to business, huh?
How can I help you?
Wow.
How straightforward you are, Commander.
Then I'll be frank about my request.
Sometimes I crawl onto the ground
to pick up some broken Rapture parts
and sell them on the Dark Net. That's what I do for a living.
Isn't that illegal?
Oh, don't be so stuck up.
Yes, it's illegal.
Of course, I know that.
But I'll starve to death if I don't keep doing it.
I hurt my leg not long ago.
I don't know how else to make a living now.
So if you could bring me some Rapture parts
from the surface, I'd be very grateful.
I won't do anything illegal.
It's easier than lifting a finger for you, Commander.
But I have to risk my life every time I go to the surface.
Get a job.
Hahahahaha.
Commander,
there are no jobs in the Outer Rim.
Then find one in the Ark.
So you don't know.
Humans that live in the Outer Rim
don't have civil rights.
We'll be shot dead the second we step into the Ark.
Sorry, what did you say?
You heard me right.
So please help me.
I've been starving for two weeks.
ಥ_ಥ
Fine. I'll help.
Ahem.
Thank you. Thank you so much.
I'll give you the exact coordinates.
If you happen to go to the surface, please don't forget about my request.
I'll be waiting for the good news. Haha.
What are you picking up, Commander?

Did copper coins fall to the ground?
They're mine, and you should give it back.
A Collector from the Outer Rim asked for my help.
Outer Rim?
Collector?
You'd better get out of whatever you're into, Commander.
The Central Government is very cautious about the Outer Rim and the people there.
The place is even seen as a base for terrorists.
I don't know how the Collector got you into this,
but if you just help him like that, it may just come back to bite you in the ass.
I want to help him.
Then I'll stop talking, but...
Be careful.
Thank you!
Thanks to you, I'm finally full.
It must be difficult for you to squeeze out the reward.
No, no.
For what you've done for me, such a reward is not even close to what you deserve.
I'll pay you back for sure.
How much can you make with it?
Food for a week.
That's not much if you have to risk your life for it.
I have no choice.
Our lives
are only worth that much.
I shouldn't bother you any longer.
Keep in touch.
*Knock knock*
Anyone there?
Long time no see.
Oh, Commander!
I'm touched that you'd remember
a nobody like me all the way from the Outer Rim.
How have you been?
It's been rough.
Doing great.
Oh, sorry to hear that.
There's a light at the end of the tunnel.
Things will get better.
Glad to hear it.
I have some good news as well,
so I wanted to send you a message.
Nothing special.
After what you did for me,
I was able to finish my treatment,
and now I can get back to work.
So no problems with the leg?
Hee-hee.
I traded it for something better.
What?
My leg was too far gone to save, so off it went!
Then the doctors swapped it for some Nikke parts
and 2nd generation parts at that! What's more, my body didn't reject them.
So it's as good as new now! Hehe.
Sounds like you've been through a lot.
Good for you.
Um...
I didn't make you uncomfortable, did I?
I'm sorry if I did.
I think it's fantastic, and I wanted to tell you about it.
This new robot leg is way better. That decrepit old leg of mine had to go.
Anyway,
would you be interested in going up to the surface with me?
Why the surface?
Why together?
I came across a promising lead.
But you've got to keep it on the down-low.
My friend told me you can make a fortune up there.
It's all above board too.
The Central Government is even encouraging people to do it.
Something's not right...
You're just skittish because you've been duped one too many times before.
I'll handle everything.
All you have to do is do me a small favor,
and you'll get yourself a sweet reward.
I need more explanation.
We can talk more up on the surface.
You can find me at these coordinates.
I'll see you there.
This doesn't add up, Commander.
Why would you go up to the surface with the Collector?
He could shoot you in the back and rob you blind.
You need to have some faith in people.
We're not talking about an ordinary individual here.
This guy is from the Outer Rim.
He'd sell his own mother to make a quick buck,
and people like him aren't exactly the law-abiding type.
Anis may be exaggerating a bit,
but people from the Outer Rim have been responsible for many violent incidents.
That includes some that were directed against Commanders.
They would put on a friendly façade and lure a Commander to the surface.
After killing them, they would steal his identification chip. Some will occasionally return to the Ark, posing as the slain Commander for several months.
But he seems like a nice guy.
Anyone can pretend to be nice for a few moments.
Anis can't.
As long as we're there, I don't think there will any problem.
But Commander,
I have to tell you...
Yes?
You shouldn't be too trusting of others.
Yeah, nice guys tend to have shorter lifespans here.
But that's what makes Master so special.
I feel the same way.
Let's head out. These coordinates aren't too far away.
Commander, over here!

I didn't think you'd actually come!
I was so worried that I barely got a wink of sleep!
Hello.
Oh, hello! So you're the Nikkes who work with the Commander?
This is my first time seeing Nikkes that weren't mass-produced!
Have I ever told you about Exotic? They're Nikkes from the Outer Rim. Practically everybody looks up to them, and...
Can we move this along?
Oh, right! Sorry, I talk too much when I get too excited.
Anyway, have a look at this.
The Collector takes something out from his coat pocket.
It is a cube that is shining brilliantly.
Do you know what this is?
... Gold?
Wow! It's so shiny!
This place used to be a bank, so you can dig up lots of these bad boys.
With your Nikkes, you'll be able to take as much as you can carry.
If you turn these in to the Central Government, they'll make it worth your while.
How about this? It's not illegal, and it's money, right??
You're from the Outer Rim, so how do you plan on turning yours in?
That's where you'll need to do me a small favor.
The Commander can submit mine for me, and give me a small percentage.
How much are we talking here?
As much or as little as you'd like.
I was hoping for at least 10%, though.
What's the catch?
What?
Is this stuff stolen or is it mixed with dangerous stuff?
I know your type. There's always a catch.
Anis.
It's all right, I can see why you'd be suspicious.
I am a citizen of the Outer Rim, after all. One without a chip.
But I'm telling you, this is all legit.
Consider it a favor to the Commander who saved my life.
C'mon, guys! Let's get digging!
Thank you, Commander.
I didn't expect you to give me over 50%!
You did right by me, so I'll do right by you.
It was nothing, really.
It was just my way of thanking you.
Actually, having too much money can be a bad thing in these parts.
Since there's no law to protect us here,
power is the ultimate currency.
Are you in any danger?
There is no safe place in the Outer Rim,
but I'm safe enough for now.
I'm able to afford protection.
Protection?
As I said,
power supersedes everything in the Outer Rim.
A group of thugs controls the area where I live,
but if I pay them off, they don't bother me.
They may end up changing their minds one day.
You're right,
but not today.
I can survive another day.
That's how life is here.
Is there anything I can do?
You must hear this all the time,
but you truly are a good person, Commander.
Thank you for everything you've done,
but as your Nikkes have told you,
bad things happen when you associate with people from the Outer Rim.
You came to my aid when I needed it most
and I returned the favor the only way I knew how.
In a sense, you could say we're even now.
Take care of yourself,
and I'll do the same.
Farewell, friend.
If the time ever comes when you need my help,
just call for me,
and I'll do everything I can.
Deal.
So long.
Have a nice life!

Hello, Commander.
This is Tetra Connect, Ark's source of entertainment.
Congratulations on graduating from the military academy.
We're wondering
if you could help us film a Tetra Connect program. That's why we're reaching out to you.
Is this a good time or...?
Sure.
Thank you.
The program name is Nikke, the Ethereal Beauty.
Many people feel sorry for Nikkes.
They look like ageless beauties that are being used as weapons to reclaim the surface.
Thus far, over 10,000 Nikkes have been sent to the surface, yet most don't make it back.
"For Nikkes who know of their destined deaths, they still head out to the surface and fight for the peace of mankind."
This is a program about them.
Are you interested?
I am.
Thank you.
It's simple.

When you go to the surface next time,
all you have to do is film them in battle.
What's your current phone model?
SAFE UP-02
Ah, Missilis' masterpiece.
Then use that phone to film.
A relatively low resolution would be more immersive.
I'll be waiting.
Filming?
I never knew you had such a hobby.
It's nothing. Why do you ask?
Tell the whole story.
... A program especially for us?
Hm... This could be interesting.
So all we have to do is to fight as dashingly as we can, right?
Heh heh...
Finally, it's time to use my ammo collection.
Rainbow bullets!
What's that?
When these bullets explode, it's rainbow-colored.
I asked the Carronades to make them.
They'll make our firepower even better.
Ah, yes. Okay.
Tetra Connect...
Huh? What's wrong?
Nothing.
Go!
Let's go!
What if they ask me to be a star because I'm too good?
I don't care.
We've received your video.

Please wait for a moment.
We're checking the content.
Momentary silence.
Ah...
I'm sorry. We can't use this.
Why not?
The battle went too well,
and they won. Ugh.
We should have told you this before, but...
I want a video where Nikkes lay down their lives.
Sorry, come again?
I told you that many people in the Ark feel sorry for Nikkes.
They won't feel sorry if Nikkes don't lose their lives,
and it is only if Nikkes have fallen to their demise miserably.
Please make sure you capture some death scenes next time.
Oh, right!
It'd be nice to interview the Nikke before she meets her end.
Please inform me when you have a dying Nikke so we can prepare for the interview.
Until next time, then.
Hello, {AccountData.NickName}.
I'm an operator of the Central Government's Intelligence Department.
We have an urgent task for you.
An urgent task?
42 hours ago, a Commander ran away to the surface.
The Commander doesn't pose any danger as she's currently unarmed.
Since she's a Commander, any information about the Ark is at the risk of being leaked if a Rapture captures her.
Please get her back as soon as possible.
Why did she run away?
I can't answer that.
I'm sending you the target's information and estimated coordinates.
We'll be waiting for your good news.
... They didn't give me a choice. I'll go to the coordinates.
Are you sure she's here? I only see the Rapture.
... Huh?
There's something under your foot, Rapi.
Rapi picks up a handbook.
... It's the Commander's certification.
Woah, the Commander really ran away?
Why?
Who knows?
She can't stay on the surface alone for long anyway.
Perhaps she's dead by now.
Let's search around this area.
Not a good idea. We don't have any operators or supplies.
Let's head back.
I've received your report.
It's a shame you didn't find her.
The runaway Commander will be marked as killed in today's operation.
Thanks for your hard work.
Who is that Commander anyway?
Why do you ask?
Just curious.
Her name was Jane Miller.
She became a Commander three years ago, and has lost every battle since.
She had recently failed again, and the Central Government was planning to dismiss her from her post.
What does that have to do with her runaway?
I don't know.
Commanders don't necessarily lose their jobs after being dismissed.
The Central Government usually gives most of them
new jobs that are more suitable for them.
So the dismissal would be an illogical reason for her to run away.
In any case, there's no way of knowing the truth now.
Anyway, we've talked about it for long enough,
now it's time for me to knock off.
Goodbye.
Hello, {AccountData.NickName}.
I'm an operator of the Central Government's Intelligence Department.
I'm not reaching out to you for an urgent task.
Instead, it's a personal request.
Personal request?
Not long ago, something strange was caught on a surface-based drone.
It looked like something sneaking around with a hood on,
and it looked very much like a human.
Everyone in the company dismissed it as a bag moving with the wind,
but I'm certain that it's a human.
Why?
The way it moved looks very familiar.
Also, a Commander by the name of Jane Miller
was considered dead after attempting to run away. Ring any bells?
Could it be...
It was moving just like her
and it just so happens that the location is close to where she disappeared.
If possible, can you investigate the area once more?
But of course, it could be my misjudgment...
I'll look into it.
Thank you.
This is a personal request, so the company can't know about this.
I'd appreciate it if you can keep this a secret.
Can't it be a formal request?
Normally, it could.
But so far, searching for missing persons
results in failure 90% of the time.
And the other 10% of the time, they find a dead body.
Unless there's a valid reason like last time,
it's highly unlikely to convert it into a formal task.
I see.
I'm sending you the coordinates.
Please find her.
She can't be alive.
Anis.

Am I wrong?
How long can a human survive being on the surface?
Nothing like that has ever happened.
Vital signs detected ahead.
What?!
... What?
At our eleven o'clock, Commander.
Something with a hood on is looking right this way.
Grab her!
Yes, Commander.
Is it real?
Let's go!
The ground begins to shake.
Raptures! Seems like an ambush!
Ugh! Seriously?
Let's eliminate them with intense firepower!
Enemy neutralized.
Where'd she go?

... We lost her.
There's no signal, so we can't determine her location.
Ugh, I'm exhausted.
... But we did get something out of this.
There's a glowing blonde hair on Anis' hand.
She really is alive.
Let's head back, Commander.
We now have a lead.
I see. Let's go.
What a surprise.
I've received your report.
She really is alive.
That's good.
Do you know each other?
What?
You sound like you know the runaway Commander.
I do know her.
I was practically her exclusive operator.
We've been through many battles together
and had an emotional connection.
Actually,
I didn't think she'd run away.
She was the type that tried her best, no matter how incompetent she might be.
I can't figure out why she'd run away so suddenly.
Anyway, now that I know she's still alive,
I can always ask her why when I see her next time.
Now, I just need to figure out what to do next.
When I do, may I ask for your help again?
Of course.
Thank you.
Until next time.

Then what?

Midtown's facilities will be restored one by one.

I see. I'll try reactivating it.
SYSTEM: Standing by...
The power is back on.
But can the city be restored just like that?
Ghost is actually Enikk's prototype.
Functions like city management and restoration are reliable.
The surface was a paradise. Each city had its own AI.
Is that why we want to get the surface back as soon as possible?
I suppose. The Ark is good, but the surface is even better.
Even if the cities get restored, I don't think we can move back to the surface right away.
No, because of the Raptures.

What a waste,
to restore these uninhabitable cities.
It won't make much of a difference.
No matter what, I still think it's worth the effort.
Me, too.
Same here.
At least there is still hope that's worth fighting for.
I agree.
Believing in this kept me alive.
The Central Power Center is now running.
From now on, you can give orders to restore Midtown.
However, you can't execute other orders when the restoration is in progress.
Please keep in mind that the restoration will be interrupted if you enforce another order.
Thank you.
If everything is clear, do you want to start the restoration now?
Start the restoration.
Confirmed.

Hello, Commander.
You've helped out so much on the surface!
So, I'm here with something very, very interesting.
I'm a Treasure Hunter, btw.
Something very interesting?
Oho.
Seems I've already piqued your interest, huh?
Do you like treasure, Commander?
I've got with me here a treasure map!
No matter how much I look at it, it doesn't seem to be anywhere in the Ark.
It has to be on the surface...
But I can't go to the surface for now.
For now?
Anyway...
I heard you're such a competent Commander
that you'll agree to any request.
How about we find this treasure together?
How's that? Still interested?
If we can find the treasure,
and I mean IF,
we'll split it 50-50.
That's too much!
I'm the one with the treasure map, after all!
